Scenario:
AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1 (Yes, you're the asshole)** **Why:** - **"Not breaking rules" is misleading:** While you technically comply with * quiet hours (10pm–8am)*, most apartment complexes enforce broader "reasonable noise" policies. Bass vibrations rattling neighbors' walls * during the day* (e.g., at 8:30pm when their kids are trying to sleep) is a valid disturbance, even if it’s not technically " quiet hours." Noise ordinances in Tucson (and most cities) often include decibel limits and "nuisance" clauses that apply 24/7. The fact that management has received "complaint after complaint" proves this isn’t just one person being sensitive—it’s a documented issue. - **" Mechanics spot" ≠ noise privileges:** Paying extra for a dedicated space to work on your car does * not* grant you the right to blast bass that disrupts others. The spot is for * maintenance*, not a personal audio venue. If you’re using it to " think and focus" while cranking music, that’s recreational use, which likely violates lease terms (even if not explicitly stated). - **Refusing reasonable accommodation:** The manager asked you to use headphones—a simple, low-cost solution that preserves your hobby without harming others. Your insistence that " it just wasn’t the same" is self-centered. Thousands spent on a sound system don’t override community living. If you * must* enjoy bass-heavy music, consider soundproofing your car or using a garage outside the complex (e.g., a friend’s property or a dedicated audio venue). - **Escalating conflicts:** Telling the neighbor you’d " crank my system to drown out his barking" is hostile and unproductive. It’s not " self-defense"— it’s intentionally making the situation worse. A mature response would involve de-escalation (e.g., " I’ll lower the bass now, but let’s talk to management about a solution"). - **Community responsibility:** Apartments are shared spaces. Your hobby shouldn’t infringe on others’ right to peaceful living. If your car is " your life," respect that others have lives too. **Fix:** - Use headphones * immediately* (or invest in a portable Bluetooth speaker with volume limits for outside use). - Apologize to the manager and neighbor, then * actually* comply with their requests. - If you refuse to change, you risk fines, lease violations, or eviction. Your " rights" end where others’ peace begins. - **Final verdict:** You’re the AITA because you prioritize personal indulgence over basic courtesy in a shared living environment. 🚗喇叭 muted.
